newsitem.title: MAURITIUS: Mauritius sees sugar output at up to 620,000 tonnes.
newsitem.headline: Mauritius sees sugar output at up to 620,000 tonnes.

text.p: The Mauritius Sugar Syndicate on Thursday forecast Mauritius 1997 sugar production at between 600,0000 and 620,000 tonnes.

"My forecast is based on favourable climatic conditions which prevailed during the first three months of this year, which are normally known as the cyclonic period of the year," Syndicate Director Michel Hardy told Reuters.
Hardy said he expected the Mauritius Chamber of Agriculture to make its 1997 forecast in May ahead of its harvest season, normally between June and December.

Mauritius produced 589,000 tonnes of sugar in 1996, lower than a preliminary forecast of 610,000 tonnes made by the Syndicate in May of that year. Production was adversely affected by cyclonic weather in December 1995 and February 1996.
The Syndicate exported 34,927 tonnes of sugar during January 1997 against 70,380 tonnes during December 1996 and 83,835 tonnes during January 1996, Syndicate officials said.
They added that out of the 34,927 tonnes, 34,124 tonnes was consigned to European Union countries and 275 tonnes to the United States. The remaining 528 tonnes went to the world market.
